Obsidian buys human-inspectable backlinks and graph view for free but does not buy temporal edge validity, point-in-time queries, or automatic supersede-edge creation — the things "latest always wins over multi-year horizons" actually needs — and those are wiring gaps a vault alone won't close (RESEARCH.md:350-351 already catalogs zep/graphiti temporal-KG and basic-memory Obsidian-native as known alternatives).

audit_summaries.summary: The memory metabolism splits cleanly into two tiers: deterministic shell hooks (session briefs, heartbeat, workflow-state, index touch, log GC) which demonstrably ran as designed, and everything requiring either a headless `claude -p` spawn or an operator-installed scheduler — which has a 100% lifetime failure rate. Dream has NEVER succeeded (6/6 spawns since 2026-05-28 died with "Not logged in · Please run /login"), the instinct-extraction middle stage has failed on every invocation including three today, and the compaction witness died the same way, leaving a checkpoint "(pending)" for 38 days. None of the four local schedulers (dream-cron, atlas-refresh, gc-nightly, overnight backstop) were ever installed (.claude/state/routines-installed does not exist; crontab and LaunchAgents empty), so the 38-day laptop-off gap (Jun 15 23:08 → Jul 23 19:04 in session.log) produced zero maintenance. Critically, the design's only response to detected staleness is warning strings at SessionStart — it never auto-runs the cheap deterministic refreshers (initiative-state.sh sync, atlas-refresh.sh, memory-rollup.sh) that would fix them in seconds, and two bookkeeping bugs (dream success recorded regardless of failure; reading `.last_run` when the writer emits `last_run_epoch`) make dream failure both self-hiding and permanently displayed as "never". Freshness is therefore entirely operator-dependent today; a single change — SessionStart executing the deterministic sync scripts instead of printing warnings, plus a hard health-check on the headless claude path — would make most of it self-healing.
